To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a novel method for sensitive measurement, in exhaled breath condensation (EBC), of seven metabolites involved in "Arginine-Asymmetric dimethylarginin (ADMA) cycle" has been developed.

a new online trapping and enrichment UPLC-ESI-MS/MS system, coupled with a simple specimen preparation, was developed and successfully applied for the first time to measure ADMA in EEC of asthmatic and cystic fibrotic adolescents.
we developed an analytical method for the simultaneous quantification of arginine, ADMA and SDMAs in EBC samples, using a novel online enrichment system coupled with an UHPLC-MS method.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a sensitive and selective analytical method for the quantification in EBC of the seven metabolites involved in the arginine-ADMA pathway.
the development of a novel analytical method for the simultaneous quantification of "Arginine-Asymmetric Dimethylarginine cycle biomarkers" in EBC.
a new analytical method to detect arginine-ADMA metabolites in EBC.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
this method is suitable for the quantification of arginine, ADMA and SDNA in EBC.
the proposed method is a reliable, sensitive and specific approach to measure the "Arginine-Asymmetric Dimethylarginine Cycle" metabolites in EBC.
this analytical method is a useful and reliable tool for the quantitation of ADMA and SDMAS in EBC, and it is suitable for clinical studies.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed an online sample trapping, enrichment and UPLC-ESI-MS/MS for the simultaneous quantification of arginine, ADMA, SDMA and Tyr.
the proposed method could represent a valuable tool for clinical studies and for the investigation of the "Arginine-Asymmetric Dimethylarginine Cycle" biomarkers in EBC.

the proposed method is an innovative approach for the simultaneous measurement of seven metabolites in EBC, and it can be considered as an alternative to the classical invasive method, which is still the gold standard for ADMA measurement in biological fluids.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the developed method can be successfully applied to measure arginine-ADMA metabolites, in EBC of asthmatic and cystic fibrosic patients, in order to better characterize the pathophysiological mechanisms involved in the development of these diseases.
the developed method can be used for simultaneous quantification in EBC of seven metabolites involved in "Arginine-Asymmetric dimethylarginines" cycle.

the proposed online sample enrichment and trapping UPLC-ESI-MS/MS approach can be used as a powerful tool for simultaneous determination of ADMA and related metabolites in EBC, with a good accuracy, precision and sensitivity.
